## Troubleshooting HP OfficeJet Pro 9015e on macOS
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/printer.svg
It sounds like your HP OfficeJet Pro 9015e is having trouble being recognized by your MacBook Air via USB. This diagnostic checklist will guide you through common solutions to get your printer installed and working on macOS Sonoma 14.4.

### Printer Connection Diagnostic Checklist

| Step | Action | What to Check | Expected Result |
| :-- | :--- | :---------- | :-------------- |
| 1 | **Verify Physical Connections** | Ensure the USB cable is firmly plugged into both the printer and a functioning USB-C port on your MacBook (possibly using a hub/adapter if needed). Try a different USB port or adapter. | The printer should be powered on and might show a connection indicator. |
| 2 | **Power Cycle Printer and Mac** | Turn off the HP printer, unplug its power cable for 30 seconds, then plug it back in and turn it on. Restart your MacBook Air. | Printer reinitializes; macOS reloads, clearing temporary glitches. |
| 3 | **Test USB Cable** | If you have another USB A-to-B printer cable, try using it. Faulty cables are a common cause of connection issues. | Rules out a defective cable. |
| 4 | **Reset Print System on Mac** | Go to `System Settings > Printers & Scanners`. Right-click (or Control-click) on any empty area within the printers list and select `Reset Printing System...`. Confirm the action. | This removes all printers and their drivers, often resolving underlying system conflicts. |
| 5 | **Install Latest HP Drivers** | Visit the official HP support website for the OfficeJet Pro 9015e. Download and install the latest macOS drivers and software specifically for your printer model and macOS Sonoma. | Ensures your Mac has the most compatible software for the printer. |
| 6 | **Manually Add Printer** | After resetting the print system and installing drivers, return to `System Settings > Printers & Scanners`. Click the `+` button. Wait a moment to see if the HP OfficeJet Pro 9015e appears in the list. Select it and click `Add`. | The printer should now be discoverable and successfully added to your Mac. |
| 7 | **Consider Wi-Fi Connection** | If USB continues to fail, connect your printer to your Wi-Fi network (via the printer's control panel). Then, in `System Settings > Printers & Scanners`, click `+` and try to add the printer over the network (it should appear as a Bonjour or IP printer). | Provides a reliable alternative connection method if USB issues persist. |
